decisions.decision: Two services in one monorepo, same stack: (1) gateway service (payment core: accounts, wallets, payments + ledger, refunds/disputes, merchant REST+gRPC, risk scoring, transactional notifications; owns its Postgres schema and the outbox) and (2) ops-ai service (projections, search, assistant/agents, alerts, tickets; own schema). They talk only through the D-013 ops port: events (outbox -> Redis Streams), gateway query API, gateway command API (routing override). No shared tables, no cross-service imports. Each service may run api / worker processes. Ledger atomicity stays inside the gateway.
decisions.why: Makes positioning B (D-012) and the tiered failure behavior (D-011) real in code, allows independent scaling (evaluation criterion: scalability), and matches the brief's 'microservice' deliverable without splitting the sync auth path.
decisions.supersedes: Earlier proposal: one platform service run as api/grpc/worker processes.
decisions.cost: Service-to-service auth and startup wiring, estimated ~half a day.

decisions.decision: Deterministic tools compute facts and money; LLM parses NL into typed filters, picks tools, and narrates. Settlement narration is generated from a verified typed breakdown.
decisions.why: Numbers must never be invented; also gives an evaluable boundary.

decisions.decision: Postgres unique (merchant_id, idempotency_key) + request hash as source of truth; stored response replayed; Redis is only a fast path.
decisions.why: Redis loss must not allow a double charge.

decisions.decision: Transactional outbox in the payment DB transaction -> relay -> Redis Streams -> consumers with dedupe by event id.
decisions.why: Without it a crash between commit and publish loses confirmations and fraud alerts (raised by Sol).

decisions.decision: Both API validation (Pydantic / protobuf + business rules) and AI guardrails (tenant scope from auth only, tool allowlist + typed args, retrieved text untrusted, abstain on weak evidence).
decisions.why: The brief's wording is ambiguous; covering both is safer for a 'missing item = fail' rule.

decisions.decision: Redis session (TTL, merchant-isolated) + last N turns + structured conversation state; long-term = explicit auditable merchant_memory written only via confirmed tool call, with source turn id, correct/delete. No silent LLM fact extraction.

decisions.topic: Product purpose, users, mandatory capabilities, scope
decisions.decision: Purpose: safe and reliable payments; when a payment fails, is declined, looks fraudulent or settles differently than expected, merchants and operations staff decide cause and response with evidence and act within safe limits. Primary users: merchants and operations staff; consumers use payment functions; financial institutions are counterparties. Mandatory = the 13 Basic items only, in 6 groups (payment core B1-B3, merchant integration B8, risk B7, operations intelligence B4-B6/B9/B10, operations workflow B11-B12, interfaces B13). Ledger / zero double charge / card-testing detection are kept as design choices or verification scenarios, not requirements. No real money movement; Advanced and NFRs are not part of the purpose; scale/compliance reported as demonstrated vs production-design-only.
decisions.why: The Overview's last sentence is a capability list, not a purpose; it drops the problem (failures, fraud, settlement) and the users the sample queries come from.

decision.thesis: Explain payment outcomes with evidence, and guide the next safe step.
decision.entry_points: A question (primary; all 4 sample queries) or an alert (secondary; shown with card testing), both into one investigation flow. Proactive failure-rate anomaly detection kept light (not Basic).
decision.loop: Investigate (ranked hypotheses with evidence, data-as-of, gaps; SQ1 also shows alternative hypotheses and when NOT to reroute) -> Respond (approved routing override, or ticket/notification with evidence pack) -> Verify (time-ordered replay; 'recovery observed', never 'effect proven') -> Learn (AI layer only; human verdicts go to a separate feedback set; golden eval set stays frozen).
decision.routing_override_safety: Applied conditionally on config version + operation id; TTL expiry reverts only if the config is still at the version it set.
decision.tiers: Failure-behavior classification, not an availability guarantee. T0 must not stop: gateway sync path, no LLM. T1 may delay, must not lose: outbox (retained, replayable) / stream / settlement / notifications, plus AI-layer deterministic parts (projections rebuildable from Postgres, alert rules, ticket routing) that work without an LLM. T2 may degrade: LLM diagnosis/assistant falls back to dashboards + evidence list with retrieval time (no NL fallback).
decision.authorization: Tenant and role checked at every stage (retrieval, history, tool call); instructions inside merchant documents never grant permissions.
decision.claims: Every tier/region claim labeled demonstrated vs production-design-only. Data residency claim covers the LLM provider: prompts minimized, provider regional terms verified before any claim.
decision.unchanged: Stablecoin not the core (design-only rail at most). Home region per account, production design only; AI projections in the same home region.
decision.design_doc: Keeps a Basic 13-item mapping so payment features are not hidden behind the AI story.

decisions.why: Align with D-012/D-013; critical review found the push-first loop, action-centric thesis, unsupported 'no loss' claim, eval contamination and override conflicts.
still_deferred: Agent framework incl. OpenAI Agents SDK

decisions.decision: Narrate as a payment-operations AI layer that attaches to any gateway through an event and tool boundary (B); satisfy Basic by also implementing the gateway as the reference implementation (A).
decisions.why: Matches the FDE job (add AI on top of a customer's existing system); Basic still requires the payment core.

decisions.decision: Ops port = 3 contracts, every one carrying merchant scope taken from caller auth (never from LLM args). (1) Events in via outbox: payment outcomes (raw provider code + normalized code + mapping version, 'unclassified' allowed; retry eligibility not normalized), provider health, risk flags, settlement/payout breakdowns, config/routing/rule/deploy changes; each with event id, schema version, occurred_at, entity version; token id + BIN/last4 only, no PAN, minimal PII. (2) Reads: thin AI-side projections (search documents, investigation aggregates; no ledger/balance copies); authoritative point lookups via gateway query API; answers state data-as-of time and gaps; time coincidence with a change is a hypothesis, not a cause. (3) Commands: one only - routing override for new payments, scoped to a route, with TTL; approval token bound to operation, target, tenant, expiry; gateway re-validates current state and permission at execution. Other responses go to humans via tickets/notifications. Never: vault/PAN, ledger writes, sync auth path, fraud rules. Card testing: real-time detection/blocking = gateway; delayed detection, investigation, alerts = AI layer. Transactional notifications = gateway; alerts and tickets = AI layer, both deduped. Normalized taxonomy belongs to the port; adapters normalize. Adapter capabilities filter the tools exposed to the LLM. No AI-to-gateway learning channel for now. One codebase; boundary enforced by an import-rule test.
decisions.why: Positioning B needs a real, enforced boundary; panel will attack stale-observation actions, so the gateway is the enforcement point.
decisions.supersedes: Earlier stance that AI may propose retrying definitive failures (removed).

decisions.decision: Thin hand-rolled tool loop on the OpenAI Responses API behind an LlmPort protocol; max 6 tool calls and 20 s budget, then T2 fallback; tool schemas generated from Pydantic; tool allowlist by role and adapter capability. Deterministic mock implements the same port (wiring proof only); a real-API run of the 4 sample queries is reported separately with date and model. OpenAI Agents SDK reconsidered only for Advanced multi-agent.
decisions.why: Deterministic tests and mock parity; explicit guardrails; avoids framework lock-in on a 5-day timeline.

decisions.decision: Answer contract: the LLM returns claims[] {kind: fact|hypothesis|cause|action, text with slots, evidence_refs[]}; slot values rendered from referenced tool outputs, never typed by the LLM; checker rejects refs not produced this turn, scope (merchant/window) mismatch, digits outside slots; a cause claim without a baseline comparison and a timeline ref is demoted to hypothesis; on failure regenerate once, then evidence list only. Every answer carries data-as-of and gaps. Stated limit: matching numbers does not prove causation.
decisions.why: Turns the thesis (explain with evidence) into an enforceable mechanism and an eval metric.

decisions.decision: Generator emits a canonical scenario log (minor units); the brief's 16-field CSV/JSON export and the gateway import are both derived from it. A gateway backfill importer writes historical payments with balanced journals and emits outbox events with original occurred_at and origin=backfill; projection consumers apply them, side-effect consumers (notifications, alerts, tickets) skip them; historical incidents/tickets imported as state.
decisions.why: Gateway lookups (SQ2, SQ4) agree with ops-ai projections; the diagram shows the real dataset -> ingestion -> port -> AI path.

decisions.decision: Every repository function requires a Scope built from auth; cross-tenant probe tests over search, tools, session and memory. Postgres RLS is a stretch goal (only with a non-owner DB role and SET LOCAL per transaction).
decisions.why: Verifiable within 5 days; RLS without verified pool/role handling would weaken the claim.

decisions.decision: All remaining sections of docs/architecture-detail.md confirmed as written: repo layout; ledger and per-method state machines; refund+chargeback principal cap under the payment lock; sync charge path (tx1 reserves idempotency key + payment + attempt, provider call outside tx, guarded tx2, reconciler with provider acceptance deadline, 202 for async methods); SQ2 decline rule recording; settlement line items; provider simulator; identity/roles; audit; stream topics, relay, consumer dedupe, entity_version; query/command API and approval binding; ops-ai projections with query-time aggregates; hybrid search with swappable keyword side; investigation tools; memory; fraud_watch; tickets; web/ops; tested restart behavior; top-3 risks fixed first.

decisions.topic: Requirements-fit fixes to the detailed architecture
decisions.decision: B4 failure taxonomy in ops-ai (rules first, LLM fallback proposes from a closed list with confidence, low confidence -> unclassified, retryable from a deterministic policy, versioned fix playbook + RAG notes); B11 recipients (gateway 'was this you?' to cardholder/merchant, ops-ai alerts to ops staff only, both deduped); B3 history endpoints and dispute arbiter (simulated network or ops_lead; merchant submits evidence); B8 gRPC idempotency key in metadata, one validation module; no synchronous balance rows on platform accounts; funds hold for wallet debits leaving via external rails with stated invariants; observability + AI audit trail; risk dependency policy (rules only, risk_unavailable / degraded_scoring, DB down -> stop, unknown never rerouted); NFR claim wording (P99, multi-region, E2E encryption, GDPR, PCI, AML/KYC); Requirement 2 fit and fraud-pattern conflict answer; incident resolution-effectiveness fields in the dataset.
decisions.why: Review against Requirement 1/2 and NFRs found 4 Basic gaps, 3 design defects and over-claims.

decisions.topic: Production-grade design as the main axis
decisions.decision: Strict priority Basic > P0 > P1 > P2. P0 items P0-1..P0-15 (requirements-traceability.md) folded into the Basic slices as acceptance criteria. Key choices: Redis SET NX is contention suppression only, Postgres unique + provider key give correctness; 'charged once' proved at the provider (simulator charge ledger); crash matrix C1-C5 with one real process kill; pessimistic row locks on user accounts in id order, platform accounts append-only; unknown never retried with a new key, past the retention window -> manual reconciliation; agent tools read-only, money moves only via gateway API with the human's JWT after explicit confirmation (no new port command); allowlisted LLM input DTO + free-text redaction + canary tests; injection fixtures; RBAC policy table with ownership/tenant tests; audit in the same tx, trigger + grants (no tamper-detection claim unless the cut-first hash chain ships); OTel traces across API/worker/LLM with trace_id as correlation id; Prometheus metrics and promtool-tested alert rules; CI with deterministic DeepEval custom metrics as gate and cross-tenant hard gate, LLM-judge only with a key; mock-derived numbers labeled. Outbox stays core (Basic), although the instruction lists it as P1. Cut order if behind: audit hash chain -> Jaeger UI -> P1.
decisions.why: The user was rejected elsewhere for 'PoC only, no production evidence'; reviewers must see production experience in code, tests, docs and demo.

decisions.topic: Rest of P1, P2 on GCP, production documents and presentation
decisions.decision: P1 adds P1-6 health/readiness/graceful shutdown, P1-7 Alembic (pulled forward to Day 1), P1-8 model and prompt pinning + fallback model + daily token budget. P1 order: P1-6, P1-8, P1-5, P1-3, P1-4, P1-2. Outbox stays Basic. P2-1..P2-8 written in docs/design.md for GCP (Spanner vs. per-region Cloud SQL, 99.999 % with error budget, PCI scope reduction with KMS/HSM, residency + crypto-shredding, canary/flags/rollback, backup/restore RTO/RPO, 100k TPS, mTLS/WORM/AML); Redis Streams locally, Pub/Sub on GCP. New docs: production-readiness.md (DOC-1), two runbooks (DOC-2, DOC-3), Decision/Why/Gave up/Alternatives format (DOC-4). Grafana added to compose for the dashboard demo. Presentation gives >=3 min to production design with 3 demos (PR-1..PR-3).
decisions.why: The full production-readiness instruction answered Q-011.
decisions.gave_up: A hand-built metrics UI (Grafana instead); Alembic as a later P1 item (moved to Day 1); implementing any P2 item; listing outbox under P1.

decisions.topic: Implementation routing, Day 1 exit criteria, submission repo
decisions.decision: No contracts-first phase. Claude builds the thin slice inline (signup -> wallet -> card charge -> ledger + outbox same tx -> relay -> ops-ai projection -> search -> mock answer, minimal success path only), fixing only the event schema, dedupe and port it needs. Then at most two lanes (G: gateway, A: ops-ai + UI), slices <= half a day with their own acceptance commands; Codex authors in worktrees, Claude reviews; auth/payment slices go through security-auditor + red-team. Owner and merge order fixed for shared deps, contracts and migrations. A wrong test is never satisfied by bending the spec: park it, ask the user at once only if it blocks, batch the rest. Day 1 exit: clean checkout -> make up + make ci green; automated proofs: concurrent same key -> provider-side call count 1, same success body for all, no duplicate ledger postings; C2 retry returns stored response; LlmPort down -> charge succeeds + assistant T2. Toolchain recovery time-boxed to 60 min (Nix devShell for python312/uv/node). Submission repo: private GitHub repository with reviewer invite.
decisions.why: Sol consult 2026-11-03: contracts-first adds coordination cost before conventions exist; integration left to the last day is the main schedule trap.
decisions.gave_up: Up-front full OpenAPI/proto and parallel workers from hour one; public repository.
